note: Condensed from runs/*/conversation.md. Every line paraphrases a real statement from the recorded runs; numbers are as the agents gave them.

acts.caption: 1 · /council:vote · real run, condensed · examples/bakery/runs/council
acts.aria: Council debate: five members vote no on online payments at launch, the skeptic finds a gap in round 2, the moderator rejects the motion and asks six questions for the client

messages.head: /council:vote Should the bakery launch with online payments or pay at pickup?
lines: Context comes from ~/knowledge: 70 pre-orders a week, 6 % no-shows, budget about 3 000 €.

messages.head: Pay at pickup. Launching on time is worth more than payments.
lines: With payments and English the build is about 4 400 €, far over her budget.

messages.head: Payments put the deadline at risk to fix a 93 € a week problem.
A deposit only for cakes sounds right to me.
lines: Refunds scare me more than the fees do.

messages.head: We all missed it: the cake deposit is taken in the shop.
lines: Cakes ordered online would skip it, right before Christmas.

messages.head: Launch with pay at pickup; quote cake deposits as an option.
lines: Six claims failed the evidence check, e.g. the card fee is 0.46 €, not 0.30 €.

messages.head: Before you quote, ask Jana six questions.
lines: Is the 3 000 € with or without VAT? When do texts and photos arrive?
How many cakes were never picked up last December?

acts.caption: 2 · /office:quote · real run, condensed · examples/bakery/runs/quote
acts.aria: Quote workflow: the main session asks six scoping questions, Lucia answers, the quote builder drafts 3 600 euros, the pricing analyst and skeptic object, the builder revises to 3 500 euros

messages.head: /office:quote one-page online ordering site for a bakery, SK + EN
lines: …contact form to email

messages.head: Six questions first: each moves the price by more than 20 %.
lines: Form to email only (about 1 700 €) or pickup slots (about 3 300 €)?
Payments? An order list? Who writes the texts? Deadline?

messages.head: Pickup slots, pay at pickup, a list for the morning shift.
lines: Jana: 3 000 € excl. VAT, up to 3 500 €. Texts by 20 November.

messages.head: Draft: 72 h, 3 600 €, 100 € over her ceiling.
lines: Priced from the hours, not squeezed into the budget. Cuts are listed.

messages.head: Hours are short against the florist project's actuals.
lines: Also: Slovak VAT is 23 % since January 2025, not the 20 % in your file.

messages.head: Cancelled orders and unpaid cakes would still get baked.
lines: Nobody can cancel an order or free its slot: that was last December's 9 cakes.

messages.head: Phase 1: 3 500 € excl. VAT, launch 1 December.
lines: Photos moved to an add-on, no discount. Phase 2 (500 €) adds a 'cancelled' switch.
Quote in Slovak, in ~/knowledge. Nothing was sent to Jana.

messages.head: Only you can check: how does the site send email today?
lines: In the repo the contact form only prints to the console.

acts.caption: 3 · /crew:ship · real run, condensed · examples/bakery/runs/crew
acts.aria: Crew workflow: the planner plans, the skeptic attacks the plan, the crew asks one decision, Lucia answers, the tester finds an old crash, the reviewer requires changes twice and then approves

messages.head: /crew:ship add online ordering with pickup time slots to the bakery website
Order form, 30-minute slots, 4 orders each, pay at pickup.
lines: Slots come from the opening hours in Bratislava time, with tests for DST.

messages.head: A slot count kept in memory resets on every restart.
lines: Anyone could fill every slot, and an async route can crash Express 4.

messages.head: One decision: drop slot capacity (A) or save orders (B)?
lines: A is simpler. B needs a file store and a limit per email address.

messages.head: B: 8 per slot, orders close at 14:00 the day before.
lines: At most 3 open orders per email. The cancel link waits for phase 2.

messages.head: A repeated form field hangs the old contact form.
lines: app.ts:135 renders an array and Express 4 drops the error. One curl reproduces it.

messages.head: A short script can book out two weeks of slots.
lines: 1 920 places, no rate limit, no honeypot. Error pages also leak stack traces.

messages.head: The double-click fix now drops a changed second order.
lines: Back, change the day, submit: the customer lands on the first order.

messages.head: Approved. Two rare double-failure cases go on the follow-up list.
Ordering is built: 323 tests pass, nothing is committed.
lines: You get the diff, the test results and a commit message to approve.

messages.head: Before go-live: how is the site deployed?
lines: A per-IP limit depends on the proxy, and real email still isn't wired.
